page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1106.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1018.0, both falling into the bottom 25% tier. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing also show weak to poor performance. However, the instance leverages its 32 dedicated cores to deliver average multi-core performance. Multi-threaded benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core (23622.2) and Geekbench multi-core (8927.0), consistently rank in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth is also stable, with uncached read speeds at 99.19 GB/sec and write speeds at 49.44 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.8xlarge offers a high-density memory profile without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. This makes it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require ultra-fast local disk I/O or high single-threaded CPU speeds. The instance is well-suited for database operations, as demonstrated by its average Passmark database score of 8570.68 and Redis SET performance of 22.7 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include multi-threaded data processing, static web serving, and moderate-scale LLM inference for smaller models.
